notes: Identity assessment: complete five-page primary Research Report, What Do Cross-National Comparisons of Personality Traits Tell Us? The Case of Conscientiousness, by Steven J. Heine, Emma E. Buchtel, and Ara Norenzayan, Psychological Science 19(4), 309–313, copyright 2008. Title, authors, year and pagination match the neutral original reference. DOI is not printed in the text and was not independently resolved. Provenance names the UBC author-hosted PDF. No PDF path supplied; no acquisition used. Target: printed p. 311 (third page), Table 1 self-report NEO-PI-R row, matches all five named criteria but provides five outcome correlations under two deletion schemes and an average. Neither the description nor locator identifies one test. Table 2 on p. 312 additionally reports GDP-adjusted correlations, outside the supplied page locator. Candidate N: case-wise deletion uses 10 countries with complete data for all measures; pair-wise analyses range across 17–55 countries without individual target-cell Ns. Countries are analytic observations, distinct from contributing participants. This common case-wise N is candidate evidence only. No analytic N selected; no arithmetic derivation. Candidate effects: canonical Table 1 digit strings (pair-wise / case-wise) are postal .57 / .58; clock .34 / .39; walking .27 / .43; GDP .66 / .16; longevity .38 / .38; average .43. Narrative explicitly describes all these self-report NEO-PI-R associations as negative. Canonical parse appears to omit minus signs and misrender significance stars and equals signs; these digit strings must not be treated as verified signed coefficients. Footnote 4 documents averages calculated from r-to-Z-to-r transformations; no conversion performed here. Table 1 gives significance-marker bounds p < .05 and p < .01, with stars rendered as n; no exact p values in the table and no unique same-test bound assignable. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders, not extraction findings.
